Maimen Intel
Python 3.10+, one dependency
  1. Fetch and parse each source
  2. Flag what's new using hashed state
  3. Mask coupon codes and member IDs
  4. Split private and public views
  5. Render reports and share image

What the user gets

Private reportMarkdown and HTML
Public pagecampaigns only
Share image1080 px PNG
Xiaohongshu draftwith source link
Contains personal data, never published

Guardrails I designed in

Claiming coupons is off by default and needs an explicit confirm flag; results are verified before and after.

No write actions beyond claiming: no ordering, points spending or lucky draws.

Never fills gaps with demo data; failed or unknown data is labelled as such.

Tokens are never printed or saved, and no scheduled tasks are created.

Status: in development. Unofficial project, not a McDonald's product. Code and README at github.com/jerryhan1201-debug/maimen-intel.

Jerry Han, selected work4 / 8
Personal product, 2026, AI-assisted prototype

SameFace: turning "natural retouching" into controls

"The same person on a better day." Better-looking photos that still look like you, with a way to compare and fine-tune the result.

The problem
AI retouching tends to change who someone is. Users need to choose what changes and how much.
What I did
  • Turned edit area, strength and protected features into parameters and prompt constraints.
  • Designed the flow: upload → compare candidates → fine-tune.
Design decision
Fine-tuning regenerates from the original photo, so repeated edits don't compound drift.
Built and tested
Next.js and TypeScript on OpenAI's image-editing model; tried by 5 trial users.
3user controls: edit area, strength and identity lock

Status: working prototype, not publicly hosted. Output quality not yet formally evaluated. Open source (MIT): github.com/jerryhan1201-debug/sameface-ai

IRIS: getting trusted AI into a real research workflow

Turning "trusted AI" from a slogan into a product that research teams can explain, trace and control.

My role
Led the team's product direction and presented the overall storyline in Shenzhen; the team delivered jointly.
What I did
  • Organised the analysis around user tasks, risks and feature priorities for research writing and discovery.
  • Translated NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and regional guidance into six product controls.
Delivered
Bilingual report and presentation: four product roles, red/amber/green risk controls, eight minimum capabilities, Plan A and B, and a 12-week pilot with metrics.
6AI control gates designed into the research-writing workflow
The key trade-off: build trusted discovery and evidence first
P0
Build trust foundations

Identity and output verification, data quality, match rationale and stated uncertainty.

P1
Support institutional decisions

Admin review, consent-based contact and time-stamped evidence export.

Later
Open content community

Prove one institution, one task and one evidence standard before expanding.

Proposed 12-week pilot
Weeks 0–2Confirm client and task
Weeks 3–6Build the evidence MVP
Weeks 7–10Test discovery and trust

UQ project for New Land Group, Scenic Rim and Gold Coast, February to May 2026

New Land: who will come, and why?

Finding the priority customers, experience mix and message for an early-stage eco-wellness destination concept.

What I did
  • Designed the research framework and survey around experience perception, restoration motives, value and intent to visit.
  • Analysed 492 valid responses in SPSS with factor analysis and K-means clustering; a logistic regression model reached 82.1% accuracy.
  • Used ANOVA and cross-tabs to explain segment differences and set positioning, product and channel advice.
A finding that shaped the segments
Willingness to pay did not differ significantly across segments (p = .170), so price was not used as the main basis for segmentation.
91.6%of the priority segment would consider visiting within 12 months
Would consider visiting in the next 12 months, by segment
High-value wellness and nature loversn = 119, 24.2% of sample
91.6%
Active mainstream travellersn = 184, 37.4%
81.5%
Interested but weakly motivatedn = 90, 18.3%
77.8%
Low-engagement travellersn = 99, 20.1%
52.5%

Self-reported intent within each segment, not actual visits or conversion.

Positioning

A short nature-and-wellness escape built on emotional recovery: get your calm back in a weekend.

Product and content

Bundle nature walks, light wellness, local experiences and comfortable stays; show scenery, itinerary and transport.

Channel tests

Test the value message and a weekend itinerary first, then compare channels. No paid ads run yet.

Status: research and recommendations delivered; the concept is at an early stage. Figures from the final report, May 2026.
